submission.name: ClearCue
submission.tagline: A spoken second opinion for suspicious links and pages, with risk patterns organized for review.
submission.inspiration: We wanted to help people who find technical scam warnings hard to interpret, especially when a message or webpage feels urgent. A short spoken explanation could give someone a moment to pause before sharing information.
submission.what_it_does: The prototype scans page text and domain clues for possible impersonation or pressure tactics, then presents a plain-language warning and an optional ElevenLabs narration. We also explored using Databricks to organize flagged signals for analysis, but scanning, analytics, and the voice flow are separate pieces rather than one complete extension experience.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used TypeScript, HTML, and CSS for a browser-extension interface, with Google Safe Browsing as a reputation signal and Groq for explanation experiments. ElevenLabs can narrate a warning, while a Databricks notebook was used to explore how extracted risk indicators might be grouped; that notebook does not yet feed results back into the extension.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: A few broad text rules flagged harmless pages, and reputation checks did not catch every suspicious example. We also ran out of time to connect the notebook output to the extension and to make narration state behave consistently, so the demo only shows parts of the intended flow.
submission.accomplishments: We built separate pieces for webpage signals, readable warning text, and spoken output. We are glad the project keeps its focus on helping a person understand why something may be risky instead of showing only a score.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that simple keywords do not provide enough context for reliable scam detection, and that explanation quality affects whether a warning is useful. Gemini-style language analysis and ElevenLabs voice both need to fit a controlled flow; we used AI coding and generation tools as aids, but had to review outputs and keep the components small.
submission.whats_next: We would connect the analytics work to the browser scan results and test the extension on more varied examples. We also want to improve domain context, reduce false alarms, and make the voice controls more predictable.
